text:
Marco: Quick follow-up from the control-plane separation thread. I sketched two ownership models for private VPC connectivity: (1) Redwood manages peering/attachments (cross-account role + automated routes), (2) Customer manages attachments and we publish manifests/webhooks. Need to pick defaults and cutover strategy.
Amy: My immediate worry is route-table scaling and noisy propagation. If Redwood pushes thousands of route ops during onboard we risk route bounce and hitting AWS RT limits.
Jin: One mitigation is using regional managed prefix-lists we update per-customer, then reference the PL in customer route tables. Makes swaps atomic and keeps per-route ops low. Limits: ~1000 entries/PL in a few regions and extra indirection.
Marco: Example of the managed-attachment flow (high level): create peering in customer account via assume-role, accept, then program route entries or prefix-list references.
Marco: If customers own attachments we instead emit a YAML manifest + preflight script they run. Safer but slower. Also harder to coordinate cert/cp rollover.
Amy: Cert lifecycle is key. If we control attachments we can gate cert rollover and swap routes under control. If customers control attachments we need a coordination API (signal ready, confirm).
Sam: For very large customers (>500 route-equivalents) we should recommend a transit model (TGW/partner transit) rather than per-customer peering. Less operational churn and avoid RT limits.
Jin: Cutover checklist proposal: 1) Dry-run (simulate route apply), 2) Apply to prefix-list or temp table, 3) Disable route propagation if using TGW, 4) Stage route swap, 5) Monitor metrics; rollback if health fails. Include exact AWS API backoff behavior in doc.
Amy: Spike asks: measure prefix-list update latency across 3 regions, observe propagation window, record error modes (rate-limit, partial apply, IAM denies). Also test switching from N static routes -> 1 prefix-list ref.
Marco: Operational default proposal: Redwood-managed attachments for self-serve up to 250 route-equivalents. Above that, require transit pattern or partner network. We'll add: opt-in for customer-managed attachments for compliance reasons.
Sam: Ops note: SRE wants a runbook for manual cutovers; include step to drain load and a monitoring dashboard with route-change alerts.
Jin: Metrics we should capture for each cutover: route API call count, propagation time (95p), number of route conflicts, rollback rate.
deploy-bot: Spike created: spike/prefixlist-prototype assigned to Marco, ETA 4d.
Marco: I'll draft an RFC addendum with the default, the cutover playbook, and the spike results. Will include customer-facing checklist and required IAM role template. Ping me if you want to join the spike.
Amy: +1. Also add a short FAQ for self-serve explaining expected downtime windows and the temporary role requirement.
Marco: Thanks all, will follow up with PRD and runbook.
